title: Calm-Down Corner
strapline: A go-to spot with tools and pictures for riding out a big feeling — never a naughty step, always a helping place.
intent: Children get a safe, resourced place to move through a big feeling with support, rather than being sent away.
Children learn concrete calming strategies — breathe, squeeze, look at the bottle, ask for a cuddle — they can actually use.
Children build the vocabulary of emotion, naming what they feel as a first step to managing it.
Children come to see strong feelings as normal and manageable, not shameful or dangerous.
Children move, over time, from adult co-regulation towards choosing a strategy for themselves.
implementation: Stock it with real tools: a glitter calm-bottle, soft toys, a feelings fan or poster, a squeeze cushion, and a breathing prompt.
Display simple calming steps in pictures — 'I feel big, I can breathe, I can squeeze, I can ask for help' — at child height.
Be crystal clear with the whole team and with children that this is a helping place, never a consequence or a time-out.
Co-regulate first: sit near, stay calm, name the feeling, and only offer a strategy once the storm eases — connection before direction.
Introduce and practise the tools when everyone's calm, so they're familiar before a real wobble hits.
Celebrate the using of it — 'you took yourself to calm down, that was clever' — so children own the strategy with pride.
key_questions: What are you feeling right now — can we find it on the chart?
Which tool might help — the bottle, a squeeze, or a cuddle?
Shall we do some slow breaths together?
What made you feel like that?
You calmed yourself down — how did you do it?

impact.text: Children name basic feelings in themselves and in pictures and stories.
Children talk about feelings, what caused them, and what helps them feel better.
Children regulate big feelings using strategies that work for them, with adults nearby not in charge.
Children know their own feelings have names and have at least one thing that helps them calm.
Children resolve minor conflicts increasingly reaching for words first after calming.

enhancements: A make-your-own glitter jar session so each child has a calm-bottle they helped create and feel ownership of.
A feelings check-in board children move their photo on as they arrive and through the day.
A 'breathing buddy' — a soft toy on the tummy that rises and falls — for lying-down belly breaths.
A book basket of stories about anger, worry and sadness to browse when settling.
A mirror so children can see and name the face their feeling makes.

playing_exploring: Children explore the calming tools — swirling the bottle, squeezing the cushion — discovering what soothes them.
The corner invites hands-on regulation rather than being talked at.
active_learning: Children return to the strategies that work, building a repertoire they own.
Successfully riding out a feeling and rejoining play is deeply motivating.
creating_thinking: Children connect a named feeling with a chosen strategy — the heart of self-regulation.
They begin to plan ahead — 'if I feel cross, I'll go and breathe' — generalising the tool.
